observations.note: Selected upstream cases pass on every target; not exhaustive conformance.
The native-only reduced control fails valid prefix/range/end-pointer cases. The invalid-base host divergence remains a separate policy issue.
Valid percent-i integer conversions do not recognize octal/hexadecimal prefixes. Additional failures need individual reduction and standards review.
The reduced native controls fail successful-write character counts and pushback/EOF cases; the compatibility adapters pass those cases.
Pinned musl search passes the upstream cases, including empty needles.
Checked adapters pass upstream and reduced prefix, sign, range and end-pointer cases.
Pinned musl scanner passes string and native-stream input cases; va_list implementations are exercised through the variadic entry points.
Stream formatting and character counts pass; output errors set the native error indicator. The shared va_list implementation is exercised.
Pushback passes all 256 byte values after repeated EOF, beginning-of-buffer lookahead and caller-owned buffer boundaries.
Selected upstream conversion and bounded-format tests pass.
The unchanged C assertions pass independently of the omitted BSD extension block.
Selected zero-length, alignment, overlap, bounds and byte-value cases pass; this is not exhaustive conformance.
Namespaced musl comparisons pass unsigned high-byte ordering and memory/string boundaries.
Native comparisons order byte 0x80 before 0x7f; ISO C requires unsigned-byte ordering.
The native byte comparison fails unsigned 0x80/0x7f ordering.
Selected unsigned byte ordering case passes.
Selected unsigned byte ordering cases pass.
Pinned musl additions pass ownership, bounds and independent tokenizer-state cases. Injected allocation failures set ENOMEM through the NeXT allocator bridge.
Native-stream line input passes embedded NUL, growth, delimiter, EOF, argument/read errors and injected allocation-failure checks.
Maximum-width conversions, range errors, quotient/remainder and j-format round trips pass on the four ILP32 targets.
Copied values, overwrite policy, repeated replacement, duplicate removal, invalid names and externally replaced environ are tested.
The native C90 week-number cases and modern calendar conversions fail independent 400-year expectations.
Musl C-locale formatting passes unchanged upstream cases and independent 400-year expectations. Other locales retain the native implementation; native time_t is unchanged.
Native line-buffered update-stream writes can return success without setting output mode, causing fflush to discard the output; read-only writes can omit the error indicator.
Native FILE bridges pass full/line/unbuffered cases, seek/update transitions, output after EOF, direct element counts, stdin scanf/vscanf and write errors.
Native empty-needle searches fail the unchanged upstream cases on all four targets.

next_batches: Review remaining missing interfaces against real application needs and native equivalents.
Expand filesystem, math and locale behavioral coverage independently; do not infer support from link availability.
Keep Unicode locales, wide stream I/O and kernel epoch-width changes outside the current single-byte library contract.
